reason: Use Tier 2: add a learned item-bias component to NextItNet scoring. Independent residual blocks reached HR@10=0.650, while feature gating fell to 0.630; this motivates testing the scoring representation instead of further convolutional complexity. The current dot product must represent both item popularity and sequence compatibility, a plausible limitation with sparse histories that an explicit learned bias can address.

plan.model_design: Start from the best 0.650 ungated, independently parameterized, residual-scaled NextItNet parent and make one atomic change: add self.item_bias = nn.Embedding(itemnum + 1, 1, padding_idx=0), initialized entirely to zero. This introduces a sequence-independent item preference learned through the frozen host's BPR objective, allowing the causal convolutional representation to focus on sequence compatibility without using external popularity statistics. In forward, add self.item_bias(pos).squeeze(-1) and self.item_bias(neg).squeeze(-1) to the corresponding dot-product scores; in score_candidates, add self.item_bias(candidates).squeeze(-1) to scores before the existing single-sequence return handling, preserving broadcasting for shared and per-sequence candidate lists. Preserve existing variable names, constructor, forward, encode_sequence and score_candidates signatures, output shapes, the eight numeric constants, parent architecture and initialization, padding masks, and last-nonpadding selection; retain exactly the permitted imports and two classes with methods only. Use one candidate slot for host-owned validation against 0.650 under the unchanged protocol, retaining the modification only for a strict HR@10 improvement, with no model-side training, evaluation, printing, file/network access, or CSV operations.
